findings.text: §21's done-when counts calls of `routing.record_names_worktree` "during one `_held_worktree_records` call" and bounds them by records plus trees, but that call also runs the whole-ledger fallback at `reckon/crew/obligations.py:586-589` (`for record in ledger.runs(...): for worktree in unresolved: if _names_worktree(...)`), which the section's own Why leaves unchanged ("stays §23's"); every inspected tree no source names adds `len(ledger.runs) × |unresolved|` counted calls, and the run §21 cites shows that fallback firing inside `_held_worktree_records` (its `fleet_state_subprocess_callers.log` records one `ledger.py runs` call at 8.146 s under obligations.py:519), so on a fixture holding two or more trees no record names the head exceeds the records-plus-trees bound by the fallback alone

findings.text: §24's headline head bound ("the first call's median on the node-local copy is at most 10 s") is justified as "§21, §22 and §23 each bound part of it", but §24 inherits §20's harness of calling `obligation_snapshot.fleet_state` directly to dodge the sweep's due gate, while §23's deliverable grants its single ledger-index build and per-run reviewed-head resolution to "every reader in the sweep" and states "Readers outside a sweep keep their current behaviour" — so the review-and-ledger share of the first call, the largest item §23 targets, is not observable on the path §24 times
